name: rBet v 1
crossReactivityDetails: Cross-reactivity with other PR-10 allergens (e.g., apple, hazelnut, celery).
description: Marker of primary sensitization to birch. Associated with pollen-food allergy syndrome.

name: rBet v 2
crossReactivityDetails: Profilin, a panallergen. Cross-reactivity with numerous pollens and plant foods.
description: Minor cross-reactive allergen (profilin). AIT is not indicated if this is the only positive marker.

name: rAra h 8
crossReactivityDetails: PR-10. Cross-reactivity with birch pollen (Bet v 1) and other plant foods.
description: Associated with local reactions (oral allergy syndrome). Low risk of systemic reaction. Heat labile.

name: rCor a 1
crossReactivityDetails: PR-10. High cross-reactivity with birch pollen (Bet v 1).
description: Associated with local reactions (oral allergy syndrome), heat labile. Low risk of systemic reaction.

name: rGly m 4
crossReactivityDetails: PR-10. Cross-reactivity with birch pollen.
description: Associated with oral allergy syndrome in birch pollen allergic patients. Heat labile.

name: rAra h 1
crossReactivityDetails: 7S storage protein, stable.
description: Risk marker for systemic reactions to peanut.

name: rAra h 2
crossReactivityDetails: 2S albumin storage protein, very stable.
description: High-risk marker for severe systemic reactions to peanut. Stable to heat and digestion.

name: rCor a 14
crossReactivityDetails: 2S Albumin storage protein, heat stable.
description: Marker of primary hazelnut allergy, associated with a high risk of severe systemic reactions.

name: rPru p 3
crossReactivityDetails: LTP. Risk marker for systemic reactions to plant foods, especially in the Mediterranean.
description: Major peach allergen, LTP-type. Heat stable, associated with severe reactions.

name: nArt v 3
crossReactivityDetails: LTP. Cross-reactivity with other pollen and food LTPs (e.g., Pru p 3 from peach).
description: LTP-type allergen, associated with LTP syndrome.

name: rAra h 9
crossReactivityDetails: LTP. Cross-reactivity with other foods containing LTPs (peach).
description: Cross-reactivity marker (LTP). Associated with local or systemic reactions. Heat stable.

name: rCor a 8
crossReactivityDetails: LTP. Cross-reactivity with other LTPs (peach).
description: Cross-reactivity marker (LTP). Associated with local or systemic reactions in sensitized patients.

name: rTri a 14
crossReactivityDetails: LTP. Cross-reactivity with other LTPs (peach).
description: LTP-type allergen, associated with baker's asthma or food allergies.

name: rFel d 1
crossReactivityDetails: Cat specific. Uteroglobin.
description: Major cat allergen, produced in salivary and sebaceous glands. Indication for AIT.

name: rFel d 2
crossReactivityDetails: Serum albumin. High cross-reactivity with other albumins (dog, horse, pork). Associated with pork-cat syndrome.
description: Minor cat allergen. Rarely clinically relevant on its own but can indicate cross-reactivity with other animals or meats.

name: rFel d 4
crossReactivityDetails: Lipocalin. Cross-reactivity with Can f 6 (dog) and Equ c 1 (horse).
description: Major allergen, associated with severe asthma symptoms.

name: rCan f 1
crossReactivityDetails: Lipocalin. Moderate cross-reactivity with other animal lipocalins like Fel d 7 (cat).
description: Major dog allergen, marker of primary sensitization. Indication for AIT.

name: nCan f 3
crossReactivityDetails: Serum albumin. High cross-reactivity with other albumins (cat, beef).
description: Minor allergen, seldom of clinical importance. Cross-reactivity marker.

name: nBos d 6
crossReactivityDetails: Bovine serum albumin (BSA). Cross-reactivity with beef and other animal albumins.
description: Minor milk allergen. May cause cross-reaction with beef. Heat-sensitive.

name: nGal d 5
crossReactivityDetails: Livetin/alpha-livetin. High cross-reactivity with bird serum albumins (bird-egg syndrome).
description: Marker for bird-egg syndrome. Sensitization to livetin can cause respiratory symptoms upon exposure to birds.

name: rDer p 10
crossReactivityDetails: Tropomyosin. Invertebrate panallergen, high cross-reactivity with crustaceans (shrimp) and molluscs.
description: Cross-reactivity marker. If dominant, a food allergy (seafood) should be investigated.

name: rPen a 1
crossReactivityDetails: Tropomyosin. Invertebrate panallergen (mites, other crustaceans, insects).
description: Major shrimp allergen, heat-stable. Responsible for cross-reactions with other crustaceans and mites (Der p 10).

name: Alpha-Gal
crossReactivityDetails: Carbohydrate. Cross-reactivity among all non-primate mammalian meats.
description: Alpha-Gal Syndrome (AGS). Responsible for delayed allergic reactions (3-6h) to red meat, often after a tick bite.

name: rHev b 6.02
crossReactivityDetails: Hevein. Associated with latex-food syndrome (banana, avocado, kiwi).
description: Major allergen in healthcare workers, marker of latex-food syndrome.

name: rHev b 11
crossReactivityDetails: Class 1 chitinase. Associated with latex-fruit syndrome (banana, avocado, kiwi, chestnut).
description: Marker for latex-fruit syndrome. Cross-reacts with certain plant foods.

name: nAct d 1
crossReactivityDetails: Cysteine protease. Major kiwi allergen.
description: Major kiwi allergen, can cause systemic reactions.

name: rPhl p 1
crossReactivityDetails: Specific to group 1 grasses. Low reactivity outside this group.
description: Major and specific allergen of timothy grass and other grasses. Indication for AIT.

name: rPhl p 12
crossReactivityDetails: Profilin, panallergen. Cross-reactivity with numerous pollens and plant foods.
description: Minor allergen (profilin) which can lead to cross-reaction.

name: rAlt a 1
crossReactivityDetails: Specific to Alternaria.
description: Major marker of sensitization to Alternaria. Risk factor for severe asthma. Indication for AIT.

name: nMUXF3
crossReactivityDetails: Carbohydrate epitope from bromelain. Marker for cross-reactive carbohydrate determinants (CCD).
description: Positivity indicates sensitization to CCDs, which is often clinically irrelevant and can cause false positives in IgE tests.
